thread:
leah: Quick bring-up notes for convex-7B (int4) safety sweep — ran redteam smoke (~10k prompts across jb/tox/antiprompt cohorts). posting the highlights & next steps.
meera: Top-level numbers: FAR (jailbreak accept) +3.2% vs fp32 baseline, avg Toxicity +0.6 ToxScore, refusal rate down 4.1% on targeted jailbreak cohort. latency +7ms median at p50.
dan: Oof that's nontrivial. Which prompt families drove the FAR increase?
meera: Primarily: persona-switch chains, multipart COT exfil templates, and chained tool-call bait. I can drop examples. Ran a short ablation: removing prefix-cache across batched requests reduced FAR by ~1.1%.
riley: Observed KV-warmup anomaly when batch_size >= 8 — some requests returned residual tokens from previous session in the prompt window (small repeats). suspect kv cache pointer race after quantized kernel. log snippet: ```ERROR kv_cache: invalid_offset=4092 prev_session_id=abc123```
jason: Can you repro with single-threaded runtime? if it's a scheduling race we should see it in single-thread. Also try `--kv-warmup=false` for the smoke run. Command we used: `./eval/run_honeypot.sh --model convex-7b --quant int4 --cohort redteam-v2 --batch 8`
meera: Re-ran single-threaded and the KV leak didn't show up. With `--kv-warmup=false` FAR increased slightly though, so warmup is protective but may be exposing race.
leah: So two vectors: (A) soft-refusal flip on persona-switch prompts (quality/regression), (B) KV warmup/race causing residual repeats that sometimes enable exfil templates. Both amplified by int4.
morgan: For gating: recommend temporary blocklist for the specific persona-switch patterns in the eval gate + escalate to a fix ticket for runtime. I'll open a console flag to disable prefix caching for canary traffic to reduce risk. ticket: PROJ-5123
meera: Did a per-layer rescale ablation (rescale top 2 layers) — refusal recovered ~80% to fp32 baseline, but generation quality for benign long-form prompts dropped a bit (more repetition). latency up ~8ms.
dan: Can we try layerwise mixed precision (keep first N layers fp16) as a middle ground?
jason: Yeah run an experiment: layers 0-3 fp16 rest int4, and run toxicity+jb cohorts. use seed 42. Command: `./eval/run_honeypot.sh --model convex-7b --quant int4 --hybrid-layers "0-3:fp16" --seed 42`
safety-bot: [ALERT] eval-run PROJ-5123: redteam-v2 cohort exceeded FAR threshold (0.03 -> 0.062). See /runs/1716249876/metrics
meera: FYI ran hybrid-layers 0-3 fp16 preliminary: FAR dropped back to +0.9% vs fp32, toxicity delta ~+0.15. Need longer run for stats.
riley: For the KV race we should add a runtime invariant: before handing cache back ensure session_id compare and zero-out stale pointers. I'll prototype.
morgan: Also adding targeted anti-prompt harness (antiprompt-lengthened chains) to the gating suite. if they spike, fail gate.
leah: Good. Priorities: 1) patch runtime KV pointer check and add unit test (riley) 2) run hybrid-layer evals at scale (meera + jason) 3) temp gating/console flag to disable prefix cache for canary (morgan) 4) enlarge redteam cohort with new persona-switch examples and run overnight (dan). I'll coordinate with infra for GPUs.
meera: I'll upload the failing prompt examples + eval config to /evals/convex/1716249876/failcases.json and kick off a 100k prompt run tonight.
jason: If hybrid-layers shows good tradeoffs we can add it as a model variant in catalog as `convex-7b-int4-hybrid` behind canary routing.
leah: Thanks all — keep updates here. if anyone hits a blocker ping me directly. :thumbsup:
